newsitem.title: CANADA: Stentor, MCI to provide high-speed data service.
newsitem.headline: Stentor, MCI to provide high-speed data service.

text.p: The Stentor alliance of Canadian phone companies said on Thursday that it will offer a high-speed global data service to businesses in Canada through an existing alliance with MCI Communications Corp.
The new service will be delivered through Concert Managed Bandwidth Service (Concert MBS), a division created in 1994 by MCI and its new parent British Telecommunications Plc.

"Canadian companies that operate internationally can now enjoy the same high-speed data service quality and standards they get at home," said Bill Enns, Stentor's vice-president of data and integrated services.
"Concert MBS will help them compete by improving and streamlining communication among their offices around the world," Enns added.

Concert MBS, which is available in 19 countries, gives clients the ability to send inventory updates, pricing information, purchase orders, product designs and sales leads to offices around the world, Stentor said.
"Dealing with a cumbersome patchwork of private lines is no longer a necessity," Enns said.

The nine members of the Stentor group are: Bell Ontario and Bell Quebec, both owned by BCE Inc, BC Telecom Inc., AGT Ltd, wholly owned by Telus Corp), New Brunswick Telephone, wholly owned by Bruncor Inc), Maritime Telegraph & Telephone Co Ltd, Island Telephone Co Ltd, Newfoundland Telephone, partly owned by BCE Inc, and Saskatchewan's provincially owned SaskTel and Manitoba's recently privatized Manitoba Telecom Services Inc.
MCI shareholders on Wednesday approved the company's takeover by British Telecommunications, whose shareholders are also expected to okay the deal.
